# Results — Study 221 (Mayer-Multiple) on real BTC-USD daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim: buying when the
Mayer Multiple (price / 200-day SMA) is below 1.0 and trimming when it exceeds 2.4 earns
superior risk-adjusted returns on Bitcoin. As-of **2026-06-16**; full history from Yahoo Finance.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | N rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| BTC-USD | 2014-09-17 -> 2026-06-16 | 4,291 | `abb873462d3e` |

First 199 rows have NaN for the 200-day SMA (warm-up); valid Mayer Multiple observations: 4,092.

## Mayer Multiple distribution (2014-2026)

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Mean | 1.17 |
| Median | 1.12 |
| Std | 0.41 |
| Min | 0.48 |
| Max | 3.93 |
| % of days below 1.0 ("cheap") | 38.6% |
| % of days above 2.4 ("expensive") | 1.5% |
| % of days in neutral zone (1.0 – 2.4) | 59.9% |

The conventional "cheap" zone (MM < 1) applies to 38.6% of days — far more than the
"fire-sale" framing suggests. The "expensive" zone (MM > 2.4) is rare: only 61 days
out of 4,092 valid observations (1.5%).

## Strategy results: long-only (MM < 1.0, flat otherwise)

| Metric | Gross | Net (10 bps / turn) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Annualised return** | **+1.5%** | **+1.0%** |
| **Sharpe ratio** | +0.045 | +0.032 |
| **HAC t-stat (mean daily return)** | **+0.19** | **+0.13** |
| Time in market | 36.8% | 36.8% |
| Buy-and-hold ann. return | **+34.0%** | **+34.0%** |

HAC t-stat of +0.19 is well below the |t| >= 2 bar. The strategy earns +1.5%/yr gross
while simply holding Bitcoin earns +34.0%/yr. It spends 63% of the time flat, missing the
bulk of Bitcoin's historic trend.

## Cost sweep (long-only, MM < 1.0)

| Round-trip cost | Annualised return | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +1.5% | +0.19 |
| 10 bps | +1.0% | +0.13 |
| 50 bps | -0.7% | -0.10 |
| 100 bps | -2.9% | -0.39 |

The strategy is negative-expectancy net of any meaningful cost and never clears the
inference bar even at zero cost.

## 30-day forward returns by Mayer Multiple regime

| Regime | N days | Mean 30-day fwd log-return | Std |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Cheap (MM < 1.0)** | 1,548 | **+1.33%** | 18.2% |
| **Neutral (1.0 ≤ MM ≤ 2.4)** | 2,453 | **+6.28%** | 21.4% |
| **Expensive (MM > 2.4)** | 61 | **-6.14%** | 29.5% |

HAC t-stat (cheap vs neutral mean difference): **−2.84**

The "cheap" band actually predicts *lower* 30-day forward returns than the neutral band
(t = −2.84, reversed from the claim's direction). The signal is statistically significant —
but in the wrong direction. Bitcoin below its 200-day SMA tends to be in a downtrend;
the Mayer Multiple labels this "cheap" when it is in fact momentum-negative.

## 30-day forward return by MM decile (decile 1 = lowest MM)

| Decile | MM range | Mean 30d log-return |
|---|---|--:|
| D1 (lowest) | 0.48 – 0.74 | +0.5% |
| D2 | 0.74 – 0.84 | +3.7% |
| D3 | 0.84 – 0.93 | -2.7% |
| D4 | 0.93 – 1.03 | +3.0% |
| D5 | 1.03 – 1.12 | +5.2% |
| D6 | 1.12 – 1.18 | +5.2% |
| D7 | 1.18 – 1.28 | +4.7% |
| D8 | 1.28 – 1.40 | +4.7% |
| D9 | 1.40 – 1.70 | +6.8% |
| D10 (highest) | 1.70 – 3.93 | **+10.9%** |

Monotonically rising forward returns from low to high MM deciles: price momentum beats
mean-reversion on a one-month horizon. The cheapest decile (MM = 0.48-0.74) has the
worst forward return. This is the momentum premium, not the mean-reversion signal the
Mayer Multiple claims.

## The key diagnostic: the signal points the wrong way

The Mayer Multiple claim is mean-reversion: buy low (MM < 1), sell high (MM > 2.4).
The data shows BTC's 30-day return distribution is momentum-shaped: high MM predicts
higher forward returns, not lower. The "cheap" signal fires precisely when BTC is in a
sustained downtrend, giving a negative edge on a 30-day horizon.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** HAC t-stat on the standard long-only strategy: +0.19 (gross).
  The 30-day forward-return band test shows a significant effect (t = −2.84) but
  *inverted from the claim*: cheap bands underperform neutral, not outperform.
  The Mayer Multiple has no predictive power in the direction advertised.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** +1.5%/yr gross vs buy-and-hold +34.0%/yr. Negative
  net return at 50 bps cost or higher. The strategy is flat 63% of the time,
  systematically missing Bitcoin's dominant trend.
- **Myth — BUSTED.** The "cheap below 1, trim above 2.4" framing applies static
  mean-reversion intuition to a momentum-driven asset. The decile analysis confirms
  the effect runs in the opposite direction: the highest-MM decile (most "expensive")
  produces the highest subsequent 30-day return.
